image_description: A white minibus parked on a residential street next to a brick house. The vehicle features a boxy design, a large front windshield, a destination display above the windshield, side windows along the passenger area, and standard wheels. A license plate is visible on the front bumper.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Boxy body shape noticeably shorter than a full-size bus, yet tall enough for passengers to stand or sit upright comfortably.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle clearly exhibits a compact, boxy silhouette distinct from full-size buses, with sufficient height for passenger accommodation.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large windshield and row of side windows along passenger area.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A large, single-pane windshield is prominent, and multiple side windows are visible along the length of the passenger cabin.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Height is substantial, with entrance door at front or mid-body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The vehicle has significant vertical clearance, and the entrance door is clearly located at the front right side of the body.
The door structure at the front right shows panel lines consistent with a sliding or folding mechanism typical of this vehicle class.
There is a distinct hood/bonnet section ahead of the windshield, indicating a front-engine layout.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rear flat or slightly angled panel with taillights and license plate mount.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rear of the vehicle is completely occluded by the viewing angle; only the front and right side are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: White, yellow, or company livery paint with route markings.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bus is painted white with a blue stripe/livery and features a digital destination sign, fitting the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Standard van-sized wheels with steel or alloy rims.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible wheels are proportionate to a light commercial vehicle/minibus chassis, appearing as standard steel rims.
The window configuration and overall size align with the capacity of a minibus (typically 12-16 seats including driver, but classified as compact compared to full buses).

artifact_observations.reasoning: The characters on the license plate ('B3...') appear distorted and non-standard. The kerning is uneven, and the character shapes melt into each other slightly, lacking the crisp edges of real stamped metal plates.
The text on the LED/matrix display above the windshield is illegible gibberish. While low resolution can cause this, the pattern looks more like generated noise than pixelated text.
The connection point of the right side mirror to the door frame appears slightly soft and indistinct, lacking clear mechanical mounting hardware details.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific make/model taxonomy and ensure it is not misclassified as a van or full-size bus.
To rigorously analyze the legibility and structural correctness of the text artifacts observed on the plate and header sign.
To check for edge bleeding between the white bus body and the background foliage, and to ensure wheel geometry is circular and connected properly.
To verify that the bus sits correctly on the road surface without floating or shadow inconsistencies.
To assess general sharpness and identify any subtle generative smoothness in the brickwork or foliage.

focus_areas: Text legibility on license plate and destination board
Boundary sharpness between bus body and background
Wheel geometry and ground contact shadows
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the license plate text. AI generators often fail to render coherent alphanumeric strings on license plates, resulting in 'alien' symbols. Verify if the text auditor confirms this as gibberish. Also, check if the topology auditor finds any fusion between the tires and the asphalt.
